bolo.title: The Claude Code docs read against the Command — the gap table
bolo.status: BORESIGHT v0.1, 9/23 hot — 83 doc practices boresighted against 54 command facts: 14 DONE · 10 PARTIAL · 33 GAP · 12 N/A · 14 ORGANIC · all four steps present, none skipped · zero hook gates proposed per ruling 1 · five cheapest fixes named, folding into BOLO 51's standing audit per ruling 3.

the standing audit function — the 9/23 ruling folds the Claude Code doctrine into BOLO 51's standing audit instead of a new SOP section

mantra.line: Eighty-three doc rows read against fifty-four command facts in one pass, the gap table written in the next. The vocabulary lands today; nothing else gets built until it earns its own ruling.

No hook gate goes in ahead of proof. The four steps get named in SOP §1 and every skill header — [C40] found no plan mode, [C41] found no worktree, and neither absence is grounds to bolt on a gate under ruling 1.

Severe means severe: an SOP rule with nothing running it reads PARTIAL, not DONE. Fourteen ORGANIC rows say the Command already covers the need its own way — that is a different claim than fourteen more DONEs, and this board does not blur the two.

frago.mission: Grade the Command's four-step workflow and every adjacent Claude Code practice against the docs, in order to give Chief a literal, severe gap table to rule on rather than a vibe.
frago.order: **Rule the five fixes and the gate question (Calls 1 and 2); then Claude writes the four steps into SOP §1 and the six skill headers and hands the gap rows to BOLO 51's audit.** One word each; "take the recs" closes all four.
frago.default: Silence: no gate is added; the five fixes wait; the rows sit in this table unread by the audit.

paragraphs.name: Situation
paragraphs.plain: The gap table itself, one group per doc page (A best-practices · B hooks-guide · C sub-agents · D common-workflows · E git-worktrees · F memory), one item per doc row (83 total). Status is graded severe: an SOP rule with nothing running it reads PARTIAL, never DONE; a habit-only memory rule reads the same way.

strand.last: docs.md (83 rows, what the Claude Code docs recommend) and command.md (54 rows, what the Command does today and what enforces it) were fetched and inventoried before this board was written.
strand.plan: Walk the six pages in order below; each item names its doc id, its practice, its status, what the doc says, what the Command does today (citing command.md's C-ids), and the gap or the cheapest fix.
strand.you: The four rulings that frame this read: vocabulary first, no hook gates until a skipped step is shown; the whole workflow set gets read in one pass; findings fold into BOLO 51's standing audit, no new SOP section; the NASA crew-grade layer (CDR · MS · PS · RANGE) stays, no Space Force.
strand.next: Read the six groups, then the Execution paragraph for what happens with the findings.

items.t: **A1 Manage context window as primary resource** — ORGANIC · Track context usage and reduce token consumption strategically as the window fills. · the Command: The Command keeps the main line's context small a different way: a SessionStart digest replaces raw reads [C1] and every formation front-loads a zero-token prep script [C2] before agents ever run. · No status line tracks percent-used; the substitute is structural (small inputs) rather than measured (a visible gauge).

**A2 Give Claude verification criteria** — ORGANIC · Give Claude something pass/fail (tests, builds, screenshots) so it can iterate without supervision. · the Command: Formations get pass/fail from RANGE reviewer scripts that check board structure and block on failure [C52][C53], the closest thing this repo has to a test suite. · The check is structural (keys present, links resolve) not behavioral (tests/build/screenshot), because this repo has no software to test.

**A3 Separate exploration from implementation with plan mode** — PARTIAL · Use plan mode (Shift+Tab) so Claude reads and answers without editing, then you approve the plan before execution. · the Command: No plan-mode gate exists anywhere in the Command [C40]; separation is structural instead — prep scripts and read-only specialists run before any write, and the main line only writes at the fan-in [C2][C12]. · The separation is real but implicit in formation order, not an explicit approve-before-edit gate Chief can invoke on demand outside a formation.

**A4 Provide specific context and constraints** — DONE · Reference specific files, name constraints, point to example patterns so Claude needs fewer corrections. · the Command: Every specialist's entire prompt is a script-written brief file naming exact sources and the one output file to write [C9], with a fixed named-output contract [C38]. · closed — nothing outstanding.

**A5 Use @ to reference files directly** — ORGANIC · Type @path/to/file so Claude reads it before responding, instead of describing where code lives. · the Command: The Command's equivalent is the brief file: a script names the exact source paths and pastes them in, so no one has to type @ mentions by hand [C9]. · Chief doesn't get the live @ suggestion menu inside a formation run; the brief is prepared ahead of time instead of composed interactively.

**A6 Write effective CLAUDE.md files** — GAP · CLAUDE.md loads at session start and carries persistent instructions; keep it short and pruned. · the Command: No CLAUDE.md exists at the repo root at all [C42]; only an unrelated one under ShroomsQ was found. · Session-start context comes only from the digest hook and MEMORY.md; there is no short, checked-in file naming code style, testing, or workflow rules for this repo.

**A7 Configure permissions with allowlists** — PARTIAL · Allowlist specific tools (npm, git) via /permissions to cut approval interruptions; combine with sandboxing. · the Command: Project settings preauthorize exactly two Bash patterns, `find:*` and `claude config set:*` [C50]; everything else still prompts. · The allowlist is real but thin — the routine commands this repo actually runs (python scripts, git status/diff, bash tool calls under _tools/) aren't on it, so most turns still prompt.

**A8 Use CLI tools like gh for external services** — GAP · Install and use the gh CLI; Claude knows how to open issues, PRs, and read comments with it. · the Command: Nothing in the Command's settings, hooks, or skills references gh or any PR workflow [C24][C50]. · The repo is public and commits happen every turn, but there is no path from a local autosave to an issue or PR — gh is simply unused.

**A9 Connect MCP servers for external integrations** — GAP · Run `claude mcp add` to connect MCP servers (Notion, Figma, databases) for integrated tool access. · the Command: The user-level settings file carries no MCP configuration relevant to this repo's own tooling — only effortLevel, theme, model, and one env var [C34][C51]. · Anything an MCP server would give (structured DB access, ticketing) is instead done by hand-rolled scripts per formation; no integration is missing that's currently blocking work.

**A10 Set up hooks for deterministic actions** — DONE · Hooks run scripts automatically at lifecycle points and guarantee the action happens every time. · the Command: Exactly two hooks are configured project-wide: Stop runs autocommit [C32], SessionStart runs the digest [C33], per the settings file [C31]. · closed — nothing outstanding.

**A11 Create skills for domain knowledge** — DONE · Skills in `.claude/skills/SKILL.md` give reusable domain workflows, applied automatically or invoked by name. · the Command: Seven skills are registered under `.claude/skills/`, each firing on named spoken phrases in its own frontmatter [C47]. · closed — nothing outstanding.

**A12 Define subagents for specialized tasks** — DONE · Create subagents in `.claude/agents/` with specific tools and prompts, running in isolated contexts. · the Command: Crew grades (CDR/MS/PS/RANGE) fix each formation seat by function and model [C13][C35], and every formation actually launches typed specialists per skill [C16]-[C21]. · closed — nothing outstanding.

**A13 Install plugins for bundled extensions** — N/A · Plugins bundle skills, hooks, subagents, and MCP servers into installable units; code-intelligence plugins add symbol navigation. · the Command: The Command has no plugin installed and doesn't need to package for reuse elsewhere — it is a single private repo, not distributed across projects. · Plugins solve portability across repos; this operation has one repo and already bundles behavior directly in SOP.md + skills + scripts.

**A14 Course-correct early and often** — GAP · Use Esc to stop, Esc+Esc or /rewind to restore to a previous checkpoint; tight feedback loops beat drift. · the Command: Nothing in command.md documents rewind/checkpoint use; the closest analog, autocommit, is a forward-only safety net [C23], not a mid-turn correction tool. · If a specialist or the main line drifts mid-turn, there's no documented habit of using Esc/rewind to back out cleanly — the fallback is finish-then-fix.

**A15 Use /clear between unrelated tasks** — PARTIAL · Run /clear to reset context between unrelated tasks so old context doesn't drag on performance. · the Command: The Stop hook's matcher explicitly fires on `/clear` alongside startup/resume [C32], so /clear is wired into the autosave+digest cycle when used, but nothing shows it's used as a habit between unrelated tasks. · The hook plumbing supports /clear; whether Chief actually clears between unrelated asks (vs. one long thread) isn't established by anything in command.md.

**A16 Delegate investigation to subagents** — DONE · Use subagents to keep large-scale exploration out of the main context; they report back summaries only. · the Command: Every formation's H0 prep script plus its read-only specialists keep exploration in a subagent's own context, reporting one named file back [C2][C12][C16]. · closed — nothing outstanding.

**A17 Use rewind checkpoints for safety** — ORGANIC · Every prompt creates a checkpoint; use /rewind to restore conversation, code, or both without losing work. · the Command: The Command's safety net is different: the Stop hook autocommits every turn to local git regardless of outcome [C23][C24], so any turn can be rolled back with git instead of /rewind. · Git checkpoints are coarser (one per turn, code-only) than /rewind's conversation+code checkpoints, and require a manual `git reset` rather than a slash command.

**A18 Resume conversations across sessions** — DONE · Run `claude --continue`/`--resume` to pick up where you left off; name sessions with /rename to find them later. · the Command: The SessionStart hook fires on its `startup|resume|clear` matcher and re-seeds context with the digest on resume [C31][C33], so resuming lands with the current state already loaded. · closed — nothing outstanding.

**A19 Run multiple parallel sessions** — GAP · Use --worktree to run isolated sessions in separate git checkouts so parallel edits don't collide. · the Command: No reference to git worktrees or any multi-checkout workflow appears anywhere in SOP.md, the skills, or the hooks/scripts read [C41]. · Chief is known to run two sessions at once against the same working tree; without worktree isolation those sessions can collide on the same files with no structural guard, only session-id discipline.

**A20 Run Claude non-interactively in CI pipelines** — N/A · Use `claude -p "prompt"` for CI, pre-commit hooks, or scripts, with `--output-format stream-json` for parsing. · the Command: The Command has no CI pipeline; it's a personal-ops repo run interactively, not built/tested by an external system. · Non-interactive CI mode has nothing to attach to here — there is no build or test stage this would gate.

**B1 Set up hooks for automation** — DONE · Hooks are user-defined shell commands run at lifecycle points, giving deterministic control. · the Command: Two hooks exist and run every session: Stop (autocommit) and SessionStart (digest) [C31][C32][C33]. · closed — nothing outstanding.

**B2 Use PreToolUse hooks to validate commands** — GAP · PreToolUse fires before a tool call and can block it — e.g. restricting DB access to read-only. · the Command: No PreToolUse hook is configured; the settings file has exactly two hooks and neither is PreToolUse [C31]. · Nothing can deterministically block a tool call before it runs — e.g. the no-unasked-probing rule [C3] is enforced only by habit, not by a hook that could refuse the scan.

**B3 Use PostToolUse hooks for formatting** — GAP · PostToolUse fires after a tool succeeds; use it to run formatters, linters, or notifications. · the Command: No PostToolUse hook exists [C31]; formatting/linting isn't part of this repo's toolchain (mostly markdown/JSON/python utility scripts). · A malformed JSON board or a script with a syntax error could land without any automatic check running right after the edit.

**B4 Use Stop hooks as deterministic gates** — PARTIAL · A Stop hook can block the turn from ending until a check passes, guaranteeing verification before Claude moves on. · the Command: The Command's Stop hook exists but is deliberately non-blocking: it always exits 0 so a git failure can never stop the session [C23][C24]; real gating happens elsewhere, in RANGE reviewer scripts at each formation's fan-in [C52]. · The one Stop hook that runs on every turn is explicitly not a verification gate; if it were, an autosave failure would incorrectly block the session, so this is a deliberate tradeoff rather than an oversight.

**B5 Use prompt-based hooks for judgment** — GAP · Prompt-based hooks use Claude to evaluate conditions needing reasoning, complementing deterministic script hooks. · the Command: Both configured hooks are plain shell/python scripts [C31][C32][C33]; no prompt-based hook exists anywhere. · Any judgment-call enforcement (e.g. "is this a probing scan?") currently has no hook path at all, deterministic or prompt-based — it's pure habit [C46].

**B6 Use agent-based hooks for complex validation** — GAP · Agent-based hooks delegate to a subagent for complex multi-step validation needing its own context. · the Command: No agent-based hook exists; the closest analog is RANGE, which is always a script by doctrine, never an agent, even at the fan-in [C13][C52]. · There's no hook-triggered agent validation step; the formation doctrine's own rule against agent-based checking (never a checker agent) [C15] makes this an intentional non-fit, not an oversight.

**B7 Hook events include SessionStart and SessionEnd** — PARTIAL · SessionStart fires at session begin/resume; SessionEnd fires at session termination, for setup and cleanup. · the Command: SessionStart is configured and runs the digest [C31][C33]; no SessionEnd hook exists anywhere in the settings. · Session open is automated; session close still depends on Chief saying "Oscar Mike" and the skill running by hand [C25], not a SessionEnd hook that fires no matter how the session ends.

**B8 Hook events include UserPromptSubmit and Stop** — PARTIAL · UserPromptSubmit fires before Claude processes a prompt; Stop fires after Claude finishes responding. · the Command: Stop is configured and runs autocommit [C31][C32]; no UserPromptSubmit hook exists. · Nothing can inspect or gate an incoming prompt before Claude processes it — e.g. auto-detecting a proword or garble before the turn starts has to happen in-context instead.

**B9 Hook events include PreToolUse and PostToolUse** — GAP · These events fire around tool calls, letting you validate or react to tool execution. · the Command: Neither is configured; the settings file has exactly two hooks, Stop and SessionStart [C31]. · Same underlying gap as B2/B3 — no tool-call-level hook exists at all.

**B10 Hook events include FileChanged and ConfigChange** — GAP · FileChanged fires on a watched file changing; ConfigChange fires when a config file changes mid-session. · the Command: Neither event is used anywhere; the only two hooks are Stop and SessionStart [C31]. · A change to `.claude/settings.local.json` or a board JSON mid-session triggers nothing automatically.

**B11 Hook events include WorktreeCreate and WorktreeRemove** — N/A · WorktreeCreate fires when a worktree is created; WorktreeRemove fires on removal at session exit or deletion. · the Command: The Command uses no worktrees anywhere [C41], so these events have nothing to attach to. · Moot until worktrees are adopted (see A19/E1-E3); these events only exist to hook a workflow the Command doesn't run.

**C1 Use subagents to preserve context** — DONE · Subagents run in isolated context windows; high-volume exploration stays there, only the summary returns. · the Command: Every formation keeps specialist reads out of the main line's context by design — the main line only ever reads the digest or the specialists' named output files [C1][C2][C12]. · closed — nothing outstanding.

**C2 Keep subagent descriptions under 15,000 tokens** — PARTIAL · Description tokens load at startup for delegation decisions; detailed behavior belongs in the system prompt instead. · the Command: The Command doesn't define reusable named subagents at all — specialists are generic Agent-tool calls carrying a brief file as the whole prompt [C9]; skill files themselves run 1.9–4.8 KB, well under budget by accident rather than by rule. · Nothing in command.md shows a deliberate token budget being tracked for any agent description — it's small because the format is small, not because a limit is enforced.

**C3 Enforce tool restrictions with tools field** — GAP · Use `tools:` or `disallowedTools:` so a subagent's access matches its job (read-only reviewer vs. Bash-capable fixer). · the Command: No `.claude/agents/` definitions with a `tools:`/`disallowedTools:` field are referenced anywhere in command.md; specialists are scoped by brief-file instruction ("read nothing else, write only X") [C36], not by an enforced tool allowlist. · A PS or MS specialist could technically call any tool available to the Agent type it runs under; the "read nothing else" boundary is convention, not a config-enforced restriction.

**C4 Use @ mentions to guarantee subagent delegation** — ORGANIC · Type @"agent-name" to force a specific subagent to run, bypassing automatic delegation. · the Command: The Command guarantees which agent runs a different way: each skill's H1 step names the exact agent type and pastes a brief file as its entire prompt [C36], and skills themselves fire on named spoken phrases rather than @ mentions [C47]. · The guarantee is procedural (skill text says which agent) rather than syntactic (@ mention in the message), so it depends on the operator following the skill's steps.

**C5 Set permission modes per subagent** — GAP · Use `permissionMode:` (default, acceptEdits, plan, dontAsk) to control how a subagent handles permission prompts. · the Command: No permission-mode configuration for any subagent appears in command.md; formations run under whatever the main session's permission mode is. · A PS/MS specialist doing pure fetch-and-write work still prompts (or auto-accepts) at the session's default rather than a mode scoped to its narrow, disjoint job.

**C6 Choose model for cost and performance** — DONE · Set `model: sonnet/haiku/opus` per subagent to trade off cost and capability. · the Command: Crew grades fix the model by seat every time: PS=Haiku, MS=Sonnet, CDR=Fable/main-line-only, RANGE=script-never-a-model [C13][C35], applied identically across every formation's skill text [C16]-[C21]. · closed — nothing outstanding.

**C7 Isolate subagents in git worktrees** — GAP · Set `isolation: worktree` so a subagent works an isolated repo copy and can't touch the main checkout. · the Command: No worktree isolation exists for any subagent anywhere [C41]; every specialist writes directly into the shared working tree. · A specialist that mis-writes has no structural containment — the fixed-output-contract convention [C38] is the only guard, not filesystem isolation.

**C8 Preload skills into subagent context** — ORGANIC · List skills in a `skills:` field to inject domain knowledge at subagent startup without requiring discovery. · the Command: The Command preloads a different way: the brief file itself IS the preload, pasted verbatim as the specialist's entire prompt [C9], with the boundary "read nothing else" stated in skill text [C36]. · This works for narrow, single-purpose specialists; it wouldn't scale to a subagent needing several skills' worth of standing knowledge at once, which the `skills:` field is built for.

**C9 Enable persistent memory for subagents** — GAP · Set `memory: user/project/local` so a subagent keeps a directory that survives across conversations. · the Command: No subagent in the Command has persistent memory; every specialist is one-shot with a fixed input brief and a fixed output file [C38], gone once the formation ends. · A PS/MS that runs the same kind of extraction repeatedly (e.g. EXTRACT-k in collect) starts cold every time — no accumulated pattern knowledge carries between runs.

**C10 Use PreToolUse hooks in subagents** — GAP · Define PreToolUse hooks scoped to a subagent to conditionally allow or block its operations. · the Command: No PreToolUse hooks exist anywhere in the Command, for the main session or any subagent [C31]. · Same root cause as B2/B9 — no PreToolUse hook exists to scope, whether at session or subagent level.

**C11 Organize subagent files hierarchically** — GAP · Create subfolders under `.claude/agents/` to organize agents by domain; identity comes from `name`, not path. · the Command: No `.claude/agents/` directory is referenced anywhere in command.md; specialists exist only as generic Agent-tool invocations described in skill text, never as named files on disk [C36]. · There's nothing to organize because named subagent files were never created — crew-grade identity lives in SOP prose, not in a `name:` field on a checked-in file.

**C12 Run subagents in background** — PARTIAL · Subagents run in the background in interactive sessions by default, letting you keep working while they finish. · the Command: Formations launch multiple specialists together in one message so they run independently and concurrently [C37]; this matches the platform default rather than a Command-specific setting. · Concurrent, background-style launch is described in skill text, but nothing in command.md confirms it's deliberately configured rather than just the tool's out-of-the-box behavior.

**C13 Resume subagents to continue work** — GAP · Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to resume a subagent without spawning a fresh instance. · the Command: No mention of resuming a subagent appears anywhere in command.md; every formation spawns fresh specialists per run [C16]-[C21]. · If a specialist's draft needs a second pass, current doctrine says rerun it fresh with the finding pasted under its brief [C22], not resume its own history — cheaper to write, more expensive in tokens than a true resume.

**C14 Limit subagent nesting depth** — GAP · Use `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` to cap how deeply subagents can spawn their own subagents. · the Command: No env var or setting limiting nesting depth appears in command.md; the formation rule already discourages deep nesting by having specialists report to the main line only, never spawn their own subagents [C12]. · Nesting depth isn't config-capped, only convention-capped by the flat hub-and-spoke shape; a specialist that did try to spawn its own subagent wouldn't be technically blocked.

**C15 Cap concurrent subagents** — ORGANIC · Use `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS` to prevent resource exhaustion past 20 running agents. · the Command: Gear N is the Command's own concurrency cap: gear 1 = 3 agents (default) up to gear 5 = 15 (never used), one shift per task then reverting to gear 1 [C14]. · Gear N is enforced by SOP text and habit, not a hard platform-level env var — it could in principle be exceeded if the rule were ignored.

**C16 Scope MCP servers to subagents** — N/A · Use `mcpServers:` to give a subagent access to MCP tools unavailable in the main conversation. · the Command: The Command connects no MCP servers of its own at all [C34], so there is nothing to scope to a subagent. · This depends on A9 (connect MCP servers) being true first; since no MCP server is wired in, per-subagent scoping doesn't apply yet.

**C17 Run entire session as subagent** — N/A · Pass `claude --agent <name>` or set `"agent"` in settings to run the whole session under a subagent's constraints. · the Command: Crew grades fix CDR as the main line only, by design never spawned as a subagent [C13][C35]; running the whole session as a subagent contradicts that seat definition. · Doesn't fit the doctrine: CDR's identity IS being the main line, not a subagent role that could be assumed session-wide.

**C18 Omit CLAUDE.md for lightweight subagents** — N/A · Set `omitClaudeMd: true` to launch a subagent without CLAUDE.md files, cutting context overhead. · the Command: Moot: no CLAUDE.md exists anywhere in the repo to omit [C42]. · This flag only matters once a root CLAUDE.md exists (see A6/F1's fix); until then there's nothing for a subagent to skip.

**C19 Deny specific subagents in permissions** — GAP · Add `Agent(subagent-name)` to `permissions.deny` to prevent Claude from using specific subagents. · the Command: The permissions block only lists two allowed Bash patterns [C50]; no deny list for any agent exists. · There's no config-level block on an unwanted agent type running; the only control is the main line choosing not to invoke it.

**C20 Use fork mode to inherit parent state** — N/A · A fork inherits the parent conversation's full context, tools, and history instead of starting fresh. · the Command: The formation rule requires the opposite: specialists share no state and sync only at named handoff points [C12]; fork mode's whole-history inheritance runs against that doctrine on purpose. · Fork mode solves a problem (continuing with full context) the Command's doctrine deliberately avoids creating (disjoint inputs, no shared state).

**C21 Set effort level per subagent** — GAP · Use `effort: low/medium/high/max` to override the session's effort level for a specific subagent. · the Command: Effort is fixed globally at the user-settings layer (`effortLevel: high`) [C51]; no per-subagent override is used anywhere in command.md. · Every specialist runs at the same global effort regardless of how simple its job is (a PS fetch-and-extract likely doesn't need high effort), leaving cost on the table.

**D1 Explore phase of four-step workflow** — ORGANIC · Enter plan mode (Shift+Tab) so Claude reads files and answers questions without making changes. · the Command: The explore step isn't skipped, it's just not plan-mode: a SessionStart digest [C1], per-formation prep scripts [C2], the no-unasked-probing rule [C3], and link-harvest-before-read [C4] all place a read-only pass before any write. · No literal plan-mode toggle exists [C40]; the read-before-write guarantee is structural (formation order) rather than an interactive gate Chief can invoke mid-conversation.

**D2 Plan phase of four-step workflow** — ORGANIC · Ask Claude to draft a detailed plan in plan mode; open it in your editor (Ctrl+G) to edit directly before proceeding. · the Command: Planning happens on paper instead of in an editable plan-mode doc: a DOPE SHEET carries the five-paragraph order [C6], a FRAGO patches it by script [C7], and a spoken tasking must be written into BOLO.md the same turn or it "didn't happen" [C11]. · There's no Ctrl+G-style direct edit of an ephemeral plan; the plan artifact is a persistent JSON/markdown file edited through its own formation (dope-sheet/frago), which is slower per edit but leaves a durable record plan mode wouldn't.

**D3 Implement phase of four-step workflow** — DONE · Exit plan mode, let Claude code, verify against the plan, run tests and fix failures. · the Command: Implementation runs through the formation rule (disjoint specialists, one reviewer at the fan-in) [C12], with RANGE reviewer scripts actually blocking a bad write until fixed [C52][C53]. · closed — nothing outstanding.

**D4 Commit phase of four-step workflow** — PARTIAL · Ask Claude to commit with a descriptive message and open a PR, completing explore→plan→implement→commit. · the Command: Every turn auto-commits via the Stop hook, but with a generic "autosave <date/time> · N file(s)" message [C23], never a descriptive one, and never a PR — pushing is a deliberate act kept separate from commits [C24]. · Commits happen every turn without fail, which is better-than-doc reliability, but the messages carry no information about what changed or why, and there's no PR step at all.

**D5 Get quick codebase overview** — ORGANIC · Start with broad questions, then narrow down; ask about conventions, patterns, and key data models. · the Command: The SessionStart digest hook already front-loads a ~40-line overview (rack, Blocked rows, newest BOLOs, PMCS red, box probe, tree status, main effort) automatically at open [C1], instead of Chief having to ask broad-to-narrow questions. · The digest is a fixed shape, not a conversational broad-to-narrow drill-down; a genuinely novel question about the codebase still needs to be asked by hand.

**D6 Find relevant code by domain** — GAP · Be specific using project domain language; install code-intelligence plugins for precise go-to-definition. · the Command: No code-intelligence plugin is installed or referenced [C47]; domain-language search relies on grep/glob and the skill/SOP vocabulary rather than symbol navigation. · This repo is mostly markdown/JSON/python utility scripts rather than a large typed codebase, so go-to-definition matters less, but there's still no tooling for it if a script layer grows.

**D7 Fix bugs efficiently** — GAP · Share the error, ask for fix recommendations, then apply; give the reproduce command and steps. · the Command: No documented bug-fix workflow or repro-command convention appears in command.md for the many `_tools/*.py` scripts that run the formations. · When a formation script errors (e.g. `check.py` or `assemble.py` failing), there's no stated habit of pasting the exact repro command — it likely happens ad hoc each time.

**D8 Refactor code safely** — N/A · Identify legacy code, get recommendations, apply changes while maintaining behavior, verify with tests. · the Command: No test suite exists for any of the `_tools/*.py` scripts, and no refactor workflow is documented; scripts are small, single-purpose utilities rather than a codebase under active refactor. · Refactor-safety-via-tests doesn't fit single-purpose utility scripts with no behavior contract beyond "produces this one file"; RANGE reviewer scripts already catch output-shape regressions where it matters [C52].

**D9 Work with tests** — ORGANIC · Identify untested code, generate test scaffolding, add meaningful cases, run and verify. · the Command: No test files or framework exist anywhere in command.md; verification instead runs through RANGE reviewer scripts (`check.py`, `assemble.py`) that structurally validate each formation's output before it's allowed to publish [C52][C53]. · This covers structural correctness of generated boards, not general code correctness — a genuine software test suite for the python utilities themselves still doesn't exist.

**D10 Create pull requests step-by-step** — GAP · Summarize changes, generate a PR, then refine the description; use `--from-pr` to find linked sessions. · the Command: No PR is ever created — commits stay local by design and pushing is treated as a separate, deliberate act [C24]. · There is currently no path from a batch of autosave commits to a reviewable PR, even though the repo is public.

**D11 Handle documentation** — ORGANIC · Identify undocumented code, generate docs (JSDoc/docstrings), review for standards, request examples. · the Command: The Command's documentation IS its operating model: SOP.md (57 KB) declares itself canonical [C43], each SKILL.md opens by naming the SOP section it runs [C48], and every BOLO gets a standing DOPE SHEET [C6]. · This covers process/doctrine documentation extensively; it does not cover docstrings or inline comments for the `_tools/*.py` scripts themselves, which the doc's practice is actually aimed at.

**D12 Work in non-code folders** — DONE · Claude Code works fine in notes vaults or markdown collections; .claude/ sits alongside other tools' configs. · the Command: This is already the Command's native shape — SOP.md, BOLO.md, and every board are markdown/JSON, not application code [C6][C47]. · closed — nothing outstanding.

**D13 Work with images in codebase** — GAP · Drag, paste, or path images to Claude for error analysis, UI matching, schema work, or component generation. · the Command: No image-based workflow is described anywhere in command.md for this repo's operations. · If a board or a design needed visual review (a screenshot of a published sit-rep page, say), there's no stated convention for handing Claude the image.

**D14 Reference files and directories with @** — ORGANIC · Use @file or @directory to include content directly; can reference multiple files and MCP resources at once. · the Command: Brief files serve the same purpose — a script names and pastes the exact sources a specialist needs [C9] — rather than Chief typing @ mentions live. · Multi-file/MCP-resource referencing in one live @ gesture isn't available this way; the brief has to be assembled by the prep script ahead of time.

**D15 Run Claude on recurring schedule** — GAP · Use Routines (cloud), Desktop scheduled tasks, GitHub Actions, or /loop for recurring runs with explicit success criteria. · the Command: No recurring/scheduled automation is referenced anywhere in command.md — every formation is triggered by a spoken phrase, not a clock. · Nothing runs on its own cadence (a nightly digest refresh, a weekly RTB sweep); every run needs a live prompt from Chief.

**D16 Ask Claude about its own capabilities** — N/A · Claude has built-in access to its own documentation and can answer questions about Claude Code's features. · the Command: This is a platform capability, not something the Command configures or could be missing. · Not an operational practice of the Command; it's a base Claude Code feature independent of this repo's setup.

**D17 Resume previous conversations** — DONE · Run `--continue` for the most recent session or `--resume` to choose from a list; sessions persist locally. · the Command: The SessionStart hook's `startup|resume|clear` matcher re-seeds the digest on resume [C31][C33], so a resumed session opens with current state already loaded. · closed — nothing outstanding.

**D18 Run parallel sessions with worktrees** — GAP · Use `--worktree feature-auth` for an isolated session on its own branch, useful for Writer/Reviewer patterns. · the Command: No worktree usage exists anywhere in the Command [C41]; Chief's two-at-once sessions run without this isolation. · Same underlying gap as A19/E1/E2 — parallel sessions currently share one working tree with no filesystem-level collision guard.

**D19 Delegate research to subagents** — DONE · Say "use a subagent to investigate X" to keep exploration out of the main conversation; it reports a summary. · the Command: Every formation's prep script plus disjoint specialists do exactly this on every run [C1][C2][C16]. · closed — nothing outstanding.

**D20 Pipe Claude into scripts** — N/A · Run `claude -p "prompt"` non-interactively for CI, pre-commit hooks, or batch processing. · the Command: No non-interactive/headless pipeline exists; the Command has no CI to pipe into. · Same underlying absence as A20 — there's no external pipeline stage this would feed.

**E1 Create isolated worktrees with --worktree flag** — GAP · Run `claude --worktree feature-auth` for a parallel session in its own git checkout on its own branch. · the Command: No worktree has ever been created in this repo per command.md [C41]. · Same root gap as A19/D18 — no isolated checkout exists for any parallel work.

**E2 Worktrees prevent edit collisions** — GAP · Each worktree is a separate checkout on its own branch, so a feature session and a bugfix session can't collide. · the Command: Chief runs two sessions at once against the same tree with no worktree isolation [C41]; the only guard is closing sessions by id per the parallel-sessions memory rule, which command.md doesn't independently confirm. · Two live sessions editing the same files at once have no structural collision guard — only operator discipline (closing by session id) stands between them and a stomped edit.

**E3 Monitor parallel sessions from one screen** — GAP · Use the Desktop app or `claude agents` to manage multiple local sessions visually, each optionally in its own worktree. · the Command: No mention of the Desktop app or `claude agents` view appears anywhere in command.md; parallel sessions are tracked by convention (closing by session id) rather than a visual multi-session view. · There's no single-screen view of what each concurrent session is doing; state has to be inferred from STATE.md/BOLO.md separately per session.

**F1 Use CLAUDE.md for persistent instructions** — GAP · CLAUDE.md loads at session start and carries knowledge across conversations; keep it short and pruned. · the Command: No CLAUDE.md exists at the repo root [C42]; session-start context comes only from the digest hook [C33] and the user-level MEMORY.md [C44]. · There is no short, project-scoped, checked-in file naming this repo's own conventions — everything either lives in the much larger SOP.md or in cross-conversation user memory that isn't project-specific.

**F2 CLAUDE.md files can import additional files** — N/A · Use `@path/to/import` syntax in CLAUDE.md to import additional files; checked-in files let teams compound value. · the Command: Moot — there is no CLAUDE.md to import from [C42]. · This only becomes relevant once a root CLAUDE.md exists (see F1's fix).

**F3 Auto memory notes Claude's learnings** — DONE · Claude accumulates learnings automatically from corrections and preferences, complementing CLAUDE.md. · the Command: The user-level MEMORY.md index holds roughly 45 one-line rulings, each linking to its own detail file, actively used and cited throughout command.md [C44]. · closed — nothing outstanding.

**F4 Use AGENTS.md alongside or instead of CLAUDE.md** — ORGANIC · AGENTS.md provides an alternative or complement to CLAUDE.md for project conventions. · the Command: The Command's chosen equivalent is SOP.md, which self-declares itself the canonical protocol that even Claude's own agent memory mirrors and defers to on conflict [C43]. · SOP.md is one large file (57 KB) rather than a small, dedicated conventions file the way AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md are meant to be; it does the job at the cost of being loaded in full rather than pruned.

**F5 Scope rules with .claude/rules/ directory** — GAP · Use `.claude/rules/` with multiple RULE.md files to scope instructions to specific file types or contexts. · the Command: No `.claude/rules/` directory exists; SOP.md carries all standing rules as one monolithic file rather than scoped per context [C43]. · Every rule in SOP.md applies everywhere by default; there's no way to scope a rule to, say, only the `_tools/bolostatus/` boards without it being one more paragraph in the same 57 KB file.

**F6 Configure auto memory settings** — PARTIAL · Auto memory is configurable in settings; Claude writes notes based on corrections, persisting across sessions. · the Command: Auto memory is functioning (MEMORY.md has ~45 entries [C44]), but the user-level settings file doesn't show any deliberate auto-memory configuration — only effortLevel, theme, model, autoUpdatesChannel, and one env var are set [C51]. · It isn't clear whether auto-memory's settings (what gets captured, how aggressively) have ever been reviewed or tuned versus just left at default.

**F7 CLAUDE.md treats context and enforcement differently** — GAP · CLAUDE.md content is advisory, not enforced; use a PreToolUse hook instead to actually block an action. · the Command: This is the Command's central weak point: a long list of standing behavioral rules (no-unasked-probing [C3], go-means-the-order [C8], spoken-tasking-capture [C11], OUT-block format [C30], and more generally [C46]) exist only as SOP text or memory files, checked by nothing but habit each reply. · None of these rules are hook-enforced; per this read's own framing, that's not itself a problem to fix with a gate — the ruling for this BOLO is vocabulary first, no hook gates until a step is shown to actually get skipped, and this read found no step that is skipped, only steps enforced by habit rather than config.

**F8 Keep CLAUDE.md rules concise and specific** — N/A · Ask "would removing this cause mistakes?" for every line; bloated files cause Claude to ignore instructions. · the Command: Moot for CLAUDE.md itself since none exists [C42]; the analogous question hasn't been asked of SOP.md's 57 KB or MEMORY.md's ~45 entries [C44]. · No CLAUDE.md exists to prune; the comparable pruning discipline for SOP.md/MEMORY.md is out of scope for this specific doc practice.
